text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: HOW TO MAKE IT AND HOW IT FITS

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Cut a 177 mm length of 16 mm bright bar; chamfer both ends 1 mm.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: From the chain-side end: file a 1 mm flat 0 to 12 mm (sprocket set

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: screw), 34.5 to 46.5 mm and 165 to 177 mm (bearing set screws).

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Drill a 6.5 mm cross hole at 107 mm, through the centre: this takes

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: the M6 bolt that fixes the wheel hub to the axle. Drill it with the

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: hub fitted, so the holes line up.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Spacers: two 38 mm lengths of 21 x 2.5 mm tube (16 mm bore), ends

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: square; one each side of the hub, out to the bearings.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Fit: the axle turns in the two flange bearings inside the drop plates

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: and carries the wheel and the wheel sprocket with it.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Check: the axle turns freely by hand in both bearings.
